top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, KLOwen, Lightforce, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, damon ultima brackets, SmartSTL
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, rentability, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, efficiency in bracket systems, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in second and third order movements, decrease of emergencies, performance in NHS Hospital environment
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save them time or money, or that it will reduce the number of in-person appointments. They want proof that DM increases efficiency, reduces chair time, and delivers a clear financial return, especially for braces and aligner cases.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
Clinical studies and evidence on the reduction on visists with DM for Braces treatments.
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
Reduced chair time, recent studies, practice efficiencies for aligners
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, comparative studies quantifying time and cost savings across different appliances and geographies. More real-world ROI data, especially for non-Invisalign aligners and fixed appliances, should be prioritized.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnostics
top_needs.brands_and_products: SmartSTL, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, self-ligating braces
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, accuracy of scanning, occlusal assessment, class I goal, AI versus orthodontist, accuracy in detecting malocclusions, accuracy in detecting eruption of permanent dentition, accuracy with aligner unseats
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is as accurate as a human clinician, especially for detecting clinical changes or making diagnostic decisions. Some express distrust or fear of AI replacing their expertise, or doubt the reliability of SmartSTL scans.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, clinical study, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
top_needs.gap_assessment: More peer-reviewed, head-to-head studies comparing AI/SmartSTL accuracy to orthodontists and intraoral scans are needed. Evidence for specific clinical scenarios (e.g., archwire passivity, eruption detection) is limited.
